title: Traffic failsafe allocator with geo affinity and token shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We observe tail-latency spikes and customer-visible error increases when a single region experiences transient GPU pressure. Current steering policies either (a) shift traffic aggressively and lose locality (increasing latency), or (b) shed too broadly and reduce availability. Goal: implement a 'failsafe allocator' that routes requests with preference for geo affinity and latency, but gracefully degrades capacity using per-region token credits and progressive shedding by latency quantiles. The allocator should integrate with the existing circuit-breaker layer (soft quotas + hard failover), KV cache locality hints, and Dedicated capacity reservation signals. Scope: routing decision component, token credit accounting, shedding policy, unit + integration tests, console dashboards, and rollout plan. Out of scope: fundamental autoscaler changes and model-level quantization tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Routing component can compute a per-request ranked list of candidate regions based on latency SLO weight, geo affinity score, and current capacity credits
Per-region token ledger implemented: tokens decayed/earned according to configured capacity curve and observed throughput; ledger persisted to Redis cluster and instrumented

Progressive shedding policy: requests are rate-limited first by soft thresholds (prioritized hedging, reduced fanout), then by token deficit fallback which triggers deterministic shed or reroute to compatible model variant
Circuit breaker integration: soft trip emits warning and applies weighted shedding; hard trip triggers fast-failover to fallback region and increments incident metric
End-to-end tests simulate a region overload and show graceful degradation: 99th p50/p95 latencies remain within SLO budget or degrade in controlled fashion; no catastrophic error spike
Dashboard in Console displays per-region token balance, soft/hard trip counts, and per-route shed events
Runbook updated and rollback tested (can disable token shedding via runtime flag within 5 minutes)

decision_log: Chose token-credits vs fixed static thresholds because credits allow short bursts while enforcing long-term capacity fairness
Scoring: latency SLO weight prioritized for low-latency customers; geo-affinity applied as soft multiplier to reduce churn for stateful workloads
Persistence: Redis chosen for ledger because of low-latency reads/writes and existing deployment; will implement optimistic concurrency and periodic reconciler
Shedding order: prefer reducing fanout and increasing batching where applicable before hard-dropping requests to preserve correctness
Fallback variants: prefer model-variant downgrade on compute-bound overloads (eg. quantized variant) rather than cross-region hop when acceptable for customer quality profiles
Circuit-breaker layering: soft trips set via percentiles and token depletion; hard trips triggered by sustained token deficit + elevated error rate
risks: Redis ledger hotkeys under extreme churn: mitigation — sharded keys by region+tenant and rate-limit writes
Unexpected QoS regressions for latency-sensitive customers when routed away from local caches: mitigation — conservative geo-affinity weight for pinned tenants
Telemetry gaps: need to ensure sampling of shed and reroute events to avoid blind spots
Rollout risk: mis-tuned decay rates could cause oscillation between regions; mitigation — canary + conservative decay defaults
